What is Oropis?

Oropis is an open-source, cross-platform desktop chess analysis application designed for club-level players (1000–2000 ELO) who want to understand engine analysis, not just copy moves.

Most chess tools show you what the best move is. Oropis shows you why it's the best move — using a unique architecture that combines symbolic chess intelligence with AI-powered natural language explanations.

How It's Different

Traditional chess GUIs show raw engine output: evaluation numbers, principal variations, centipawn scores. This is useful for strong players but meaningless for most amateurs.

Oropis takes a fundamentally different approach:

  1. Symbolic analysis first — pure chess logic extracts features, concepts, and tactics from the position
  2. LLM as translator — an AI model translates the structured analysis into clear, level-appropriate prose
  3. Validation layer — every LLM explanation is fact-checked against the actual board state
Key principle: The LLM never sees raw engine output. It only receives structured JSON from the Chess Intelligence Layer. This prevents hallucinated variations and ensures accuracy.

Key Features

  • Chess Intelligence Layer — zero-AI symbolic analysis pipeline
  • AI Coach Mode — interactive coaching with Socratic questioning
  • Eval Swing Explainer — understand why your move was a blunder
  • "Why Not" Comparison — your move vs the engine's best
  • Multi-Engine Support — Stockfish, Leela, any UCI engine
  • Game Library — SQLite-backed with PGN import/export
  • Explanation Levels — Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Master
  • Search Tree Visualization — see how the engine thinks

Getting Started

Installation

Linux

Download the .AppImage, .deb, or .rpm from the download page.

# AppImage
chmod +x oropis_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage
./oropis_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage

# Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dpkg -i oropis_0.1.0_amd64.deb

# Fedora/RHEL
sudo rpm -i oropis-0.1.0-1.x86_64.rpm

Windows

Download and run the .exe installer. Follow the setup wizard.

macOS

Download the .dmg file, open it, and drag Oropis to your Applications folder.

Tip: Stockfish 16.1 is pre-bundled with every download. You're ready to analyze immediately — no extra setup needed.

First Launch

  1. Open Oropis
  2. Paste a PGN into the input area, or start from the default position
  3. Click through moves using the move list or arrow keys
  4. Hit the Analyze button to start engine analysis
  5. View explanations in the Explanation Panel

Keyboard Shortcuts

KeyAction
←Previous move
→Next move
HomeGo to start
EndGo to last move

Chess Intelligence Layer

The Chess Intelligence Layer is the core differentiator of Oropis. It's a multi-stage symbolic analysis pipeline written entirely in Rust — zero AI, pure chess logic.

Pipeline Overview

Given a position (FEN) and engine principal variations, the pipeline produces a complete structured analysis:

Stockfish → Feature Extraction → Concept Mapping
  → Tactic Detection → Prompt Builder → LLM → Validator

Feature Extraction

The first stage extracts raw position features from the FEN:

  • King Safety — pawn shield, open files near king, attacker count
  • Pawn Structure — islands, passed pawns, backward pawns, doubled pawns, isolated pawns
  • Open/Half-Open Files — files with no pawns or only one side's pawns
  • Weak Squares — squares that can no longer be defended by pawns
  • Outposts — squares supported by pawns that can't be attacked by opposing pawns
  • Piece Activity — mobility scores for each piece
  • Material Balance — piece counts, bishop pair detection
  • Tactical Precursors — pins, hanging pieces, fork opportunities, mate threats

Concept Mapping

Raw features are mapped to high-level chess concepts:

  • Initiative — which side has the initiative and why
  • Tempo — tempo advantages or disadvantages
  • Key Ideas — the main strategic ideas in the position
  • Plan Skeleton — immediate, 3-move, and long-term plans

Tactic Detection

Known tactical motifs are identified from position features:

Forks, pins, skewers, discovered attacks, deflections, decoys, back-rank weaknesses, overloaded pieces, removing the defender, and interference patterns.

Prompt Builder

The prompt builder creates structured JSON that is sent to the LLM. The LLM never receives raw engine output — only the structured analysis.

Validator

After the LLM generates an explanation, the validator checks it against the board state:

  • Are all mentioned moves legal?
  • Are square attacks accurate?
  • Are material claims correct?
  • Are concepts supported by the position features?
Note: If the validator finds errors, the explanation is flagged and the user is shown which claims couldn't be verified.

Coach Mode

Coach Mode transforms Oropis from a passive analysis tool into an interactive coaching experience.

How It Works

  1. A position is displayed on the board
  2. Engine analysis runs in the background (hidden from you)
  3. The AI coach asks you a question: "What would you improve in this position?"
  4. You respond with your ideas
  5. The coach evaluates your response against the structured analysis
  6. The coach guides you toward the correct ideas without just giving the answer

Explanation Levels

Coach Mode adapts its language to your selected explanation level:

LevelELO RangeStyle
Beginner< 1200Simple language, one idea per sentence
Intermediate1200–1800Names concepts, explains "why" briefly
Advanced1800–2200Strategic depth, pawn structure references
Master2200+Full technical analysis with variations

Tips

  • Don't be afraid to be wrong — the coach is designed to guide, not judge
  • Try different explanation levels to find your comfort zone
  • Use "Reveal Answer" if you're stuck — there's no penalty
  • Review coaching session history to track your progress

Engine Configuration

Oropis supports any UCI-compatible chess engine. Stockfish 16.1 is pre-bundled.

Pre-Bundled Engine

Stockfish 16.1 is included with every Oropis download. No additional setup is required.

Adding Custom Engines

  1. Download the engine binary for your platform
  2. In Oropis, open Settings → Engines
  3. Click "Add Engine" and select the binary
  4. Configure options (hash size, threads, etc.)

Engine Options

OptionDefaultDescription
Hash256 MBHash table size for the engine
ThreadsAutoNumber of CPU threads to use
MultiPV2Number of principal variations to show
DepthUnlimitedMaximum search depth

Popular Engines

  • Stockfish — strongest classical engine, excellent for analysis
  • Leela Chess Zero — neural network engine, human-like style
  • Komodo — strong positional understanding

LLM Setup

Oropis uses an LLM purely as a translator — it converts structured chess analysis into natural language explanations. You need to configure a provider.

Supported Providers

ProviderAPI KeyOfflineRecommended Model
OpenAIRequiredNoGPT-4o
AnthropicRequiredNoClaude Sonnet
OllamaNot neededYesLlama 3.1 8B

Configuration

  1. Open Settings → LLM
  2. Select your provider
  3. Enter your API key (stored securely in OS keychain)
  4. Choose a model
  5. Set your preferred explanation level

Offline Mode (Ollama)

For completely offline operation, install Ollama and pull a model:

ollama pull llama3.1:8b

Then select "Ollama" as your provider in Oropis settings. No API key needed.

Tip: Even without an LLM configured, Oropis still provides full engine analysis and structured intelligence layer output. The LLM is only needed for natural language explanations.

Game Library

Oropis includes a SQLite-backed game library for organizing and analyzing your chess games.

Importing Games

From PGN Files

  1. Click "Import" in the game list sidebar
  2. Select a .pgn file from your file system
  3. Oropis supports multi-game PGN files — all games will be imported

From Text

Paste PGN text directly into the PGN input area. Great for quickly analyzing a game from an online source.

Game Metadata

Oropis extracts and displays full game metadata:

  • Player names and ratings
  • Event and site
  • Date and round
  • ECO opening code
  • Result

Search & Filter

Use the search bar to filter games by player name, ECO code, or date range.

Export

Export any game as PGN text — copy to clipboard or save to file.
